questions.question: The Partition of Bengal (1905) was justified by the British on the basis of __________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Administrative facility**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Partition of Bengal** was announced on **20th July 1905** by the then **Viceroy of India, Lord Curzon**, and came into effect on **16th October 1905**.
 
• The British justified the partition on the grounds of **administrative convenience**, stating that Bengal, which was the largest province of British India, was becoming too large to be administered efficiently. *Hence, administrative facility was cited as the reason for the partition.*
 
• Before the partition, Bengal had a population of over **78 million**, making it difficult for the British administration to manage effectively.
 
• The partition divided Bengal into two regions: **Eastern Bengal and Assam**, with a Muslim majority, and **Western Bengal**, which had a Hindu majority.
 
• The move sparked widespread opposition, particularly from the Hindus in Bengal, who saw the partition as an attempt to divide and weaken Indian nationalism.* Hence, the partition was perceived as politically motivated rather than merely administrative.*
 
• The opposition to the partition led to the **Swadeshi Movement**, where Indians boycotted British goods and promoted indigenous products.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Partition of Bengal – Key Details:**

 
 
• The partition was carried out to create two provinces: **Eastern Bengal and Assam** (capital: Dhaka) and **Western Bengal** (capital: Calcutta).
 
• It was seen as a deliberate attempt by the British to create religious divisions between **Hindus** and **Muslims** and weaken the growing Indian nationalist movement.
 
• Lord Curzon, the architect of the partition, argued that it would improve administrative efficiency, but many believed the real intent was to curb the influence of educated Hindus who were prominent in Bengal’s politics.
 
 
 
• **Swadeshi Movement:**
 
 
• The opposition to the partition led to the launch of the **Swadeshi Movement**, where Indians boycotted British goods and encouraged the use of **indigenous products**.
 
• It also involved protests, public meetings, and the promotion of national education and Indian industries.
 
• The movement spread across the country and became a precursor to the later phases of the Indian independence struggle.
 
 
 
• **Revocation of Partition:**
 
 
• Due to widespread protests and the failure to suppress the nationalist movement, the British government decided to revoke the partition in **1911**.
 
• Bengal was reunited, and the capital of British India was shifted from Calcutta to **Delhi**.
 
 
 
• **Other Options Explained:**
 
 
• **Economic prosperity:** The partition was not aimed at economic prosperity but rather at dividing the population based on religion.
 
• **Religious harmony:** Instead of promoting harmony, the partition created tensions between Hindus and Muslims.
 
• **Spread of education:** The partition had no direct link to the spread of education and was instead seen as a move to suppress the influence of educated Bengali Hindus.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Lord Curzon:**

 
 
• He served as the **Viceroy of India from 1899 to 1905**.
 
• He was known for his imperial policies and controversial decisions, including the Partition of Bengal.
 
 
 
• **Significance of the Partition:**
 
 
• The Partition of Bengal marked the beginning of large-scale **nationalist movements** in India.
 
• It highlighted the British strategy of **divide and rule** and strengthened the resolve of Indian leaders to fight for independence.
 
 
 
• **Legacy:**
 
 
• The partition set the tone for the communal divide in India, the effects of which are still felt today.
 
• It also emphasized the importance of unity in the Indian independence movement.

questions.question: The Andaman and Nicobar Islands are separated by ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**10° N parallel**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Andaman and Nicobar Islands** are separated by the **10° N parallel**, which divides the two groups of islands geographically.
 
• The **Andaman Islands** lie to the north of the 10° N parallel, while the **Nicobar Islands** are situated to the south of this line.
 
• The **10° N parallel** acts as a natural geographical marker between these two island groups, emphasizing their distinct environmental and socio-cultural characteristics.
 
• The separation also influences the flora, fauna, and climatic conditions between the two island groups, making each unique in its biodiversity.
 
• This division is significant in terms of administration, as the Andaman Islands and Nicobar Islands are managed collectively as a union territory but maintain distinct identities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Geographical Features:**

 
 
• The **Andaman and Nicobar Islands** consist of over **500 islands**, of which only a few are inhabited.
 
• The islands are located in the **Bay of Bengal**, close to Southeast Asia, making them strategically important.
 
• They are known for their **pristine beaches, coral reefs**, and rich biodiversity.
 
 
 
• **Climate and Biodiversity:**
 
 
• The islands experience a **tropical climate** with heavy rainfall during the monsoon season.
 
• Both the Andaman and Nicobar Islands host **endemic species** of plants and animals, including rare species like the **Andaman wild pig** and the **Nicobar pigeon**.
 
 
 
• **Cultural and Ethnic Diversity:**
 
 
• The islands are home to several **indigenous tribes**, including the **Great Andamanese**, **Onges**, **Sentinelese**, and **Shompens**.
 
• These tribes have distinct cultures, languages, and traditions, often living in isolation from the modern world.
 
 
 
• **Strategic Importance:**
 
 
• The islands are of strategic importance to India due to their location near international shipping lanes and proximity to Southeast Asia.
 
• India has established a strong military presence on the islands to safeguard its maritime interests.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **10° Channel:**

 
 
• The **10° Channel** is the water body that lies along the 10° N parallel and separates the Andaman Islands from the Nicobar Islands.
 
• It is approximately **150 km wide** and plays a crucial role in shipping and navigation.
 
 
 
• **Historical Significance:**
 
 
• The islands were historically used as a penal settlement by the British during colonial times, with the famous **Cellular Jail** located in Port Blair.
 
• The islands were also occupied by the Japanese during World War II, adding to their historical importance.
 
 
 
• **Tourism:**
 
 
• The Andaman and Nicobar Islands are a major tourist destination, attracting visitors with attractions like **Radhanagar Beach**, **Havelock Island**, and **Neil Island**.
 
• Activities such as **scuba diving**, **snorkeling**, and **trekking** are popular among tourists.

questions.question: The famous Virupaksha Temple at Pattadakal was built in the 8th century by?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chalukyas**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Virupaksha Temple** located at **Pattadakal**, Karnataka, was built during the **8th century CE** under the rule of the **Chalukyas of Badami**.
 
• This temple was commissioned by **Queen Lokamahadevi**, the consort of King Vikramaditya II, to commemorate his victory over the Pallavas of Kanchipuram.
 
• The Virupaksha Temple is dedicated to **Lord Shiva** and is renowned for its Dravidian architecture, integrated with elements of Nagara style.
 
• Pattadakal, known as the "City of Crown Rubies," was the **ceremonial capital** of the Chalukya dynasty, where kings were crowned and temples were constructed to showcase their power and devotion.
 
• The temple is part of the **UNESCO World Heritage Site group** at Pattadakal, which includes several other significant monuments.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **The Chalukya Dynasty:**

 
 
• The Chalukyas were a prominent South Indian dynasty that ruled between the **6th and 12th centuries** CE.
 
• Their empire was divided into three distinct branches: the **Badami Chalukyas**, the **Eastern Chalukyas**, and the **Kalyani Chalukyas**.
 
• Their contributions to Indian art and architecture, particularly in Karnataka, are highly significant.
 
 
 
• **Pattadakal Group of Monuments:**
 
 
• The **Pattadakal monuments** are a blend of **Dravidian** (Southern) and **Nagara** (Northern) architectural styles, symbolizing the cultural exchange during the Chalukya era.
 
• The site includes **10 major temples**, with the Virupaksha Temple being the largest and most intricately designed.
 
• Other notable temples at Pattadakal include the **Mallikarjuna Temple**, the **Papanatha Temple**, and the **Sangameshwara Temple**.
 
 
 
• **Architectural Features of Virupaksha Temple:**
 
 
• The temple features a **sanctum (garbhagriha)**, a **mandapa** (pillared hall), and an ornate **vimana** (tower).
 
• It has intricately carved depictions of **Hindu deities and epics**, such as the Ramayana and Mahabharata, on its walls and pillars.
 
• The temple also has a **Nandi mandapa**, housing a statue of Nandi, the sacred bull of Lord Shiva.
 
 
 
• **Other Dynasties Mentioned:**
 
 
• **Vardhanas:** This dynasty, under rulers like Harshavardhana, was prominent in Northern India during the **7th century CE**. However, they were not involved in the construction of the Virupaksha Temple.
 
• **Vakatakas:** They were a Central Indian dynasty (3rd–5th centuries CE) known for their patronage of the Ajanta Caves but had no connection to Pattadakal.
 
• **Pallavas:** A South Indian dynasty that rivaled the Chalukyas, they are known for their magnificent rock-cut temples at Mahabalipuram, not Pattadakal.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **UNESCO World Heritage Site:** The **Pattadakal monuments** were inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in **1987** due to their architectural and historical significance.
 
• **Chalukya Architecture:** The Chalukyas introduced a unique architectural style that combined elements of North and South Indian temple designs, influencing later dynasties such as the Hoysalas.
 
• **Significance of Virupaksha Temple:** It served not only as a place of worship but also as a symbol of Chalukyan power and artistic excellence.
 
• **King Vikramaditya II:** He was one of the most powerful rulers of the Chalukya dynasty and is celebrated for his military victories and cultural contributions.
